metadata.title: SSPP - Secure Identity Federation (ad.utoronto.ca ADFS)
metadata.remarks: System Security Plan for the ad.utoronto.ca Active Directory Federation Services (ADFS) deployment, providing secure token exchange between institutional authentication services (Shibboleth) and Microsoft Entra ID. This system functions as a federation bridge and trust boundary enforcing institutional assurance, claims governance, and accountability.

props.name: implements-architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Implements the institutional Identity Federation architecture pattern.

props.name: inherits-sspp-template
props.remarks: Inherits all normative federation, assurance, and governance requirements from the Identity Federation SSPP template.

import-profile.remarks: Imports baseline institutional security, identity, and access control requirements.

system-characteristics.system-description: Active Directory Federation Services (ADFS) deployment acting as a secure token exchange and federation broker between the institutional Shibboleth Identity Provider and Microsoft Entra ID. This system validates inbound SAML assertions, enforces institutional policy, transforms approved claims, and issues federated tokens to downstream relying parties.

props.name: institutional-owner
props.remarks: Owns federation trust, claims policy, and service lifecycle.

props.name: technical-owner
props.remarks: Defines assurance requirements, federation controls, and monitoring.

props.name: federation-role
props.remarks: ADFS operates as a federation bridge performing assertion validation and token issuance.

props.name: authentication-source
props.remarks: Primary user authentication occurs within institutional Shibboleth Identity Provider.

props.name: assertion-consumed
props.remarks: Inbound federated assertions are received using SAML 2.0.

props.name: assertion-issued
props.remarks: Outbound tokens are issued to Entra ID and other relying parties using approved federation protocols.

props.name: claims-transformation
props.remarks: Claims mapping and transformation rules are centrally approved and version-controlled.

props.name: external-identity-assurance
props.remarks: Inbound assertions are evaluated for sufficient assurance before token issuance.

props.name: conditional-access-dependency
props.remarks: Session and access risk evaluation is enforced downstream by Microsoft Entra ID conditional access.

props.name: non-interactive-identities
props.remarks: This federation service does not issue tokens for non-interactive workloads.

props.name: logging-and-audit
props.remarks: All federation transactions are logged and forwarded to the institutional SIEM.

system-implementation.remarks: This system implements secure identity federation by brokering trust and tokens between institutional authentication systems and cloud services. It inherits federation trust, assurance, and responsibility boundary requirements from the Identity Federation SSPP template.

components.title: ADFS Federation Core
components.description: Active Directory Federation Services providing secure assertion validation, claims transformation, and token issuance.

components.title: Claims Governance and Transformation
components.description: Approved claims rules enforcing attribute minimization, normalization, and policy-aligned token content.

components.title: Federation Logging and Monitoring
components.description: Logging of assertion validation, token issuance, and federation errors.

links.text: Federation telemetry is forwarded to the institutional SIEM.

roles.title: Federation Service Owner
roles.remarks: Accountable for federation trust relationships and lifecycle decisions.

roles.title: Federation Architect
roles.remarks: Defines token exchange flows, claims mapping, and trust boundaries.

roles.title: Federation Operations
roles.remarks: Operates ADFS infrastructure and enforces approved configuration.

roles.title: Federation Monitoring and Assessment
roles.remarks: Monitors federation activity and supports investigations.

control-implementation.remarks: Controls are satisfied through cryptographically protected federation trust, strict validation of inbound SAML assertions, centrally governed claims transformation, enforced separation of responsibility between authentication and authorization, and authoritative federation logging. Conditional access enforcement is inherited downstream through Microsoft Entra ID.
